goods.name: Pearls
goods.blurb: Grown in the shallow beds off the rafts and picked by hand. An otter wedding needs three; a Veyra house will pay for thirty.

goods.name: Tide glass
goods.blurb: Otter glasswork that glows sea-green in the dark. The frogs hang it under the lily-terraces and sing to it.

goods.name: Moonfish oil
goods.blurb: Pressed from a fish that only rises on the dark of the moon. Burns clean, keeps forever, smells like a harbour.

goods.name: Coral carvings
goods.blurb: A year of somebody's evenings, cut from living reef and finished with a thumb. Otters give them and otters keep them.

goods.name: Shiny moon pebbles
goods.blurb: Smooth grey pebbles off Slate's one beach, polished by a moon with no weather. Otters give them to each other and mean it.

goods.name: Iron ore
goods.blurb: Crates of nickel-iron, dug and sorted and not much else. The engine smiths of Cinder melt it into things that go very fast.

goods.name: Engraved masonry
goods.blurb: Cut stone with the old patterns on it. The frogs build their terraces out of it and will not be talked into anything lighter.

goods.name: Medicinal herbs
goods.blurb: Cut green and bundled in the field. Half the remedies in the system start here, and the good ones do not travel slowly.

goods.name: Starfruit wine
goods.blurb: Pale and faintly sharp. Moss makes it in small runs and Veyra buys it in whole small runs.

goods.name: Glowmoss
goods.blurb: A living lamp in a jar. Cats line their tunnels with it because it needs nothing and never goes out.

goods.name: Rare riverfish
goods.blurb: Silver, quick, and only in three rivers. Worth a fortune fresh and worth an apology otherwise.

goods.name: Spare engine parts
goods.blurb: Valves, seals and struts in oiled paper. Far from any dry dock, a crate of these is the difference between a ship and a wreck.

goods.name: Weapons
goods.blurb: Emberkin house arms, crated and sealed with somebody's mark. Nobody asks what they are for and everybody knows.

goods.name: Heat-resistant plating
goods.blurb: Sheet that will sit in a cloud top all day and come out grumbling. Half the shielded hulls in the sky are wearing Cinder's.

goods.name: Refined steel
goods.blurb: Bar stock, graded and stamped. The dullest cargo in the system and the one everybody is always short of.

goods.name: Reactor coils
goods.blurb: Wound by hand over nine days by somebody who will not tell you the order. A cat mechanic will trade a ship for one.

goods.name: Fire crystals
goods.blurb: Grown in the vents and cut cold. They hold a light for a week after you take them out of the sun.

goods.name: Volcanic glass
goods.blurb: Sheets of black glass off the flows, packed in ash. Cheap on Scorch because there is nothing else on Scorch.

goods.name: Emberstone
goods.blurb: Warm to the hand a year after it comes out of the ground, and nobody on Scorch has ever explained why.

goods.name: Ember silk
goods.blurb: Woven in a heated room by people who are paid not to talk about it. This season's colour is worth twice last season's.

goods.name: Faction medals
goods.blurb: Struck in small numbers for houses settling scores in public. The metal is worth nothing; the name on it is worth a great deal.

goods.name: Precision clocks
goods.blurb: Good enough to navigate by and pretty enough to argue over. Otters buy them for the harbourmaster and then borrow them back.

goods.name: Perfume oils
goods.blurb: Small stoppered bottles in a padded case. Half the system finds them ridiculous and buys them anyway.

goods.name: Storm crystals
goods.blurb: Fished out of the cloud tops on a line, still ticking. A cat will hold one up to a lamp and go quiet.

goods.name: Advanced filters
goods.blurb: Frog-made, patient, and better than anything the inner worlds can build. They will not say how and you will not work it out.

goods.name: Ancient cider
goods.blurb: Laid down in a balloon city before anyone alive was hatched. Otters weep at it; the frogs think that is the point.

goods.name: Medicinal gel
goods.blurb: Cold, clear, and it will close a wound that nothing else will. Scorch buys it by the crate and never haggles.

goods.name: Brine amber
goods.blurb: Ammonia-sea amber with something inside it that is not quite a leaf. The frogs sell it without explaining.

goods.name: Sea-foam resin
goods.blurb: Sets hard in vacuum and stays a little soft forever. A cat with a crate of this can fix almost anything.

goods.name: Ice lenses
goods.blurb: Ground from shell ice that has never melted. You can read a ship's name off it from further than you would believe.

goods.name: Cryo fuel
goods.blurb: Drawn from under the ice and shipped in double-walled crates. Heavy, dull, and the outer system runs on it.

goods.name: Moon incense
goods.blurb: Rolled in silence by people who chose to live somewhere expensive to reach. Haven burns it by the armful at festival.

goods.name: Pilgrim beads
goods.blurb: Strung one a day for a year. A pilgrim carries them out and a pilgrim carries them back, and the ones that come back cost more.

goods.name: Ancient frog tea
goods.blurb: Pressed into bricks longer ago than the records go. Otters have started a fashion for it, which the ascetics find funny.

goods.name: Prayer lanterns
goods.blurb: Paper, wire and a wish. They go up over the terraces at the turn of the year and Croak buys them all year round.

goods.name: Festival dyes
goods.blurb: Ground pigment in twists of waxed cloth. Cheap here, and in the wrong month worth whatever you say it is.

goods.name: Frogwood instruments
goods.blurb: Cut from a wood that only grows on one terrace, and tuned over a frog lifetime. An otter crew will fight over one.

goods.name: Salvaged ship plating
goods.blurb: Cut off whatever came in last, straightened, and stacked by thickness. Nobody on Nail asks what it used to be.

goods.name: Rebuilt thrusters
goods.blurb: Stripped, cleaned and put back together better than new by somebody who did it for the argument.

goods.name: Salvaged sensors
goods.blurb: Working, mostly. The ones that came off the Arc see further than they are supposed to and nobody sells those cheap.

goods.name: Arc fragments
goods.blurb: A hand's length of seamless Builder metal. It hums when you tap it, and the frogs will hear you coming.

goods.name: Stolen Ember weapons
goods.blurb: House arms with the marks taken off badly. Worth a great deal to the wrong people and a great deal of trouble to the right ones.

goods.name: Counterfeit faction medals
goods.blurb: Struck this morning, aged this afternoon. Good enough for a dock and not good enough for a house.

goods.name: Smuggled medicine
goods.blurb: The same gel Brine makes, in the wrong crates, at half the price and twice the risk. Scorch does not care.

goods.name: Cybernetic body parts
goods.blurb: Hands, eyes and a spine or two, packed in gel. Whisker will fit them as well as sell them and asks for cash.

cinder.name: Cinder
cinder.notes: Engine smiths; the cheapest fuel in the system straight from the refineries.

scorch.name: Scorch
scorch.notes: Mining frontier. Cheap rock, dangerous work, and the Emberkin nobody at home writes to.

veyra.name: Veyra
veyra.notes: Auction houses and money. Everything is for sale and everybody is watching who buys it.

tassel.name: Tassel
tassel.notes: The gossip hub and starting port. Big market, honest prices, terrible secrets.

slate.name: Slate
slate.notes: Dry docks and cranes. Tanks and holds are fitted here, as they are anywhere with a pump, and here they come with commentary.

moss.name: Moss
moss.notes: Farming moon, green to the shoreline. Will sell you grain and fruit and ask where you bank.

nail.name: Nail
nail.notes: Belt haven. Repairs, salvage and a bar. Match speeds and knock.

whisker.name: Whisker
whisker.notes: The shady end of the Belt. No questions, no paperwork, and a fitter who works in the dark.

arc.name: The Arc
arc.notes: Cat salvagers camped on the rim of a Builder ring, riding just beyond the Belt. No fuel; bring your own or beg.

grumm.name: Grumm
grumm.notes: Balloon cities in the cold upper clouds. The trade window for the whole frog system.

brine.name: Brine
brine.notes: Ammonia seas and floating apothecaries. Chemistry nobody else can read.

glass.name: Glass
glass.notes: Research station over an ocean under ice. They study the Builders and will talk your ear off.

croak.name: Croak
croak.notes: Retrograde and austere. Barely a market. The approach is dear on purpose.

haven.name: Haven
haven.notes: The frog capital and the outer system’s great market. No haggling; prices are exchange rates and goodwill.

maw.name: The Maw
maw.notes: No market. Something down there is still keeping station.

upgrades.name: Stock tank
upgrades.effect: The tank the ship came with (size from tuning).
upgrades.unlocks: Tassel's moons, the Belt, and a loose capture at Grumm.

upgrades.name: Long-haul tank
upgrades.unlocks: Cinder and the inward run, where the arrival is most of the bill.

upgrades.name: Deep-sky tank
upgrades.effect: Larger Δv budget again (size from tuning).
upgrades.unlocks: Grumm and Haven without counting every metre; the Arc with room to come home.

upgrades.name: Deep-dark tank
upgrades.unlocks: The Maw, and running hot anywhere you like.

upgrades.name: Stock hold
upgrades.effect: The hold the ship came with (units from tuning; the sim assumes 24).
upgrades.unlocks: One consignment at a time, and not a large one.

upgrades.name: Raft hold
upgrades.unlocks: Bulk runs that actually pay: ore and steel by the crate rather than the armful.

upgrades.name: Barge hold
upgrades.effect: Larger cargo capacity again (units from tuning).
upgrades.unlocks: A delivery and a speculation in the same hold.

upgrades.name: Barn hold
upgrades.unlocks: Ore and masonry by the barge, and a full frog gift-exchange in one trip.

upgrades.name: Gravitational sensors
upgrades.effect: See gravitational phenomena on the chart.
upgrades.unlocks: Nothing yet: the phenomena are not in the sky so far.

upgrades.name: Temperature control
upgrades.effect: The hold can carry goods that will not keep at hold temperature.
upgrades.unlocks: Rare riverfish, fire crystals, ancient cider, ice lenses, medicinal gel and smuggled medicine.

upgrades.name: Heat shielding
upgrades.effect: Survive an atmosphere skim, at a risk.
upgrades.unlocks: Nothing yet: risky aerobraking is not built.

upgrades.name: Cryo hull cooling
upgrades.effect: Carries the heat of a skim away, so the skim is safe.
upgrades.unlocks: Nothing yet: safe aerobraking is not built.

price.description: You pay base * sells.priceMul * mood * (1 - repDiscount). A port pays base * demand * (needsTempControl ? tempControlMul : 1) * mood * (1 + repDiscount/2). Nothing else moves a price: what you have sold here before does not, and how picked-over a shelf is does not. The stall's stock is the only limit on how much of a thing you can move at once, and that is limit enough.

reputation.description: Reputation is 0..10 points per species. Purchases and fuel at that species' ports are discounted by min(maxDiscount, discountPerPoint*points). Frog gifts scale with frog reputation; cat tolls fall by the same fraction.

toll.description: A Belt toll intercept takes min(cap, fraction*cargoValue) in goods, chosen by the cats; nothing if cargoValue < minCargoValue (they never take everything and never harm a ship that yields). There is nothing to hide behind: the only let-off is the cooldown, so a captain is never asked twice inside a month.

tow.description: A stranded or crashed ship is towed to the nearest port: cost = base + perAu*distanceAu, time = max(3, daysPerAu*distanceAu) days. If you cannot pay, the Tassel harbour bank fronts it and the debt is deducted from sales.

haggle.description: Otter ports: each visit rolls a uniform spread of +-spread on every price, then a haggle mini-exchange lets you keep the good end of the roll. Frogs never haggle (spread 0). Cats and Emberkin do not haggle either.

volatility.description: Daily random-walk wobble on what a port pays, amplitude by species. Emberkin markets are the most volatile. This is species character, not supply and demand: it does not remember anything you did.

speciesRules.otter: Haggle spread: every price at an otter port is rolled within +-spread, per good, per day. The roll is the whole of it — there is no haggling exchange behind it.
speciesRules.emberkin: Volatile prices: what Cinder wants this week is not what it wanted last week.
speciesRules.cat: Tolls in the Belt under strict custom (never everything, never a ship that yields). Impress a captain and a gift may follow.
speciesRules.frog: No haggling. "Prices" are exchange rates: you are paid in trade credit at the stall plus goodwill (reputation), and every visit ends with a gift.

stock.description: A stall's shelves hold a number rolled out of the good's own stock range, and they are rolled again when you come back from somewhere else. Staying at one dock and waiting does not restock it; going and trading elsewhere does. What you bought this visit is what is missing, and the price does not move as the shelf empties: the shelf itself is the limit.

demand.description: What a port pays for a good, as a multiple of its base price. Two questions: does this port want it (loved, on its buyer list, or neither), and is it out of the good's own region. Space is hard and there are few interspecies merchants, so carrying a loved good to another people is the trade the game is about; the same run inside one system is worth a fraction of it. Regions are named in the ports table: inner, home, belt, outer, deep.

sim.notes: orbitAu per port is the circular radius used for straight-line distance and Hohmann estimates; moons quote their parent’s radius.

regions.inner: The Emberkin worlds: Cinder, Scorch and Veyra.
regions.home: Tassel and its moons, Slate and Moss.
regions.belt: The Belt: Nail, Whisker and the Arc.
regions.outer: Grumm and its moons: Brine, Glass, Croak and Haven.
